title: WR-90 whose narrow wall waves, b = 10.16 + 2 sin(2πz/10) mm for four periods between 10 mm leads, a SolidCraft design with the wave an equation curve: S21 at 10 GHz, 23° behind a straight guide
source: The smooth wall itself, solved as the two-dimensional problem it is (emcraft_theory::wall::SmoothGuide): between the side walls the TE10 harmonic's potential H_x = ψ sin(πx/a) obeys the Helmholtz equation in the plane of the waving wall, ∂ψ/∂n = 0 on it; the guide mapped onto a rectangle (η = y/b(z)) with the wall exact at every quadrature point, spectral elements of degree 8 (480 along, 6 across), the ends closed by their modal conditions (24 modes) — 0.001° from 240 × 4 elements (Bayliss, Gunzburger, Turkel 1982; Jin 2014, §9.3): ∠S21 152.444°, |S11| 0.08386. Mode matching of the wall cut into steps does not serve here: each step's edge carries a singular field normal to the wall, and its answer moves with the steps and the modes alike (152.27° at 640 steps, 152.51° at 2560 with 160 modes, 152.36° at 1280 with 320), never settling within 0.2°

quantities.reason: the wall meshed as flat triangles with 2 mm tetrahedra at order 2: 152.695°, 0.25° off; E stands normal to the wall, so the facets' corners carry a singular field and the faceted wall's own answer (0.27° off with 24 chords a period, 0.07° with 48) — curved elements on the wall would close it. The same mesher on an E-plane bump of flat faces (no facets) meets this method within 0.008°
0.0817 at 2 mm: the faceted wall's reflection, as its phase
